lessonActivities.title: Time Expression Changes 🕐
lessonActivities.content:
Here's where it gets interesting! 🕐 Many learners forget that time words also change in reported speech. Let's clarify:

Direct SpeechReported SpeechExample
nowthen / at that time'I'm busy now.' → She said she was busy then.
todaythat day'I'll call today.' → He said he would call that day.
yesterdaythe day before / the previous day'I saw her yesterday.' → She said she had seen her the day before.
tomorrowthe next day / the following day'We leave tomorrow.' → They said they left the next day.
agobefore / previously'I did it ago.' → He said he had done it before.
last weekthe week before / the previous week'I traveled last week.' → She said she had traveled the week before.

The secret: Imagine you're reporting the conversation from a different time. Words like 'today' and 'yesterday' no longer make sense! 🗓️

Fun fact: If you report speech on the same day, 'today' can sometimes stay 'today'! Context matters! 📅

Pro tip: Look for time words in direct speech. If the reporting context has changed, shift them: today→that day, yesterday→the day before.
examples: Time change: 'I finished yesterday' → She said she had finished the day before.
Wrong vs Right: 'She said she is leaving tomorrow' × → 'She said she was leaving the next day' ✓
Same-day exception: 'I'm busy today' (reported same day) → He said he's busy today.
functions: Adjusting time expressions for reported context
Identifying when time expressions change vs. stay
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: Look for time words in direct speech. If the reporting context has changed, shift them: today→that day, yesterday→the day before.

lessonActivities.title: Place Expression Changes 📍
lessonActivities.content:
Time to explore another way! 📍 Just like time words, place words also shift in reported speech when the location changes.

Pattern: [Subject] + said/told + (that) + [place-adjusted clause]. Example: 'Sit here' → She told me to sit there.

Compare these:

Direct SpeechReported SpeechContext Change
herethereReporting from different location
thisthatObject is no longer 'this close'
thesethosePlural objects shift similarly
in this roomin that roomSpecific location reference changes
at this tableat that tableProximity indicator shifts

Fun fact: If you're reporting from the same location, place words may not change! 'Meet me here' → He told me to meet him here (if still here). 🗺️

Decision point: Are you in the same place as the original speaker? → Keep 'here/this'. Different place? → Shift to 'there/that'.
examples: Place change: 'Meet me here' → He told me to meet him there.
Same location: 'This is my office.' (reported in office) → She said this was her office.
Different location: 'This is my office.' (reported elsewhere) → She said that was her office.
functions: Determining when place expressions change vs. stay
lessonActivities.tips: Decision point: Are you in the same place as the original speaker? → Keep 'here/this'. Different place? → Shift to 'there/that'.

lessonActivities.title: Combined Time & Place Shifts 🕐📍
lessonActivities.content:
Ready for the next level? 🕐📍 Reporting speech often requires changing both time and place expressions together.

Formation: [Subject] + said/told + (that) + [time-shifted] + [place-shifted] + [clause]. Example: 'I'll meet you here tomorrow' → She said she would meet me there the next day.

Use this when:

Direct SpeechReported SpeechChanges Applied
'I'm busy here now.'She said she was busy there then.here→there, now→then
'We'll finish this today.'He said they would finish that that day.this→that, today→that day
'Come here yesterday.'She told me to come there the day before.here→there, yesterday→the day before
'I saw her here last week.'He said he had seen her there the week before.here→there, last week→the week before

Fun fact: Native speakers often simplify multiple shifts in casual speech—focus on clarity first! 💬

When to use: Always check for both time AND place words. If either context has changed, shift accordingly.
examples: Combined shift: 'I'll call you here tomorrow.' → He said he would call me there the next day.
Triple shift: 'I saw this yesterday here.' → She said she had seen that the day before there.
Context exception: 'I'm here now.' (reported same place/time) → He said he's here now.
lessonActivities.tips: When to use: Always check for both time AND place words. If either context has changed, shift accordingly.

lessonActivities.title: Contrast: When Expressions Change vs. Stay ⚖️
lessonActivities.content:
Here's where it gets interesting! ⚖️ Many learners shift every time/place word, but sometimes we keep the original. Let's clarify:

ExpressionChange?ExampleWhy?
todayOptional'I'm busy today' → He said he was busy today/that day.Same day = keep; different day = shift
hereOptional'Meet me here' → She told me to meet her here/there.Same place = keep; different place = shift
nowOptional'I'm leaving now' → He said he was leaving now/then.Immediate reporting = keep; later = shift
yesterdayUsually'I saw her yesterday' → She said she had seen her the day before.Always shifts unless reporting same day

The secret: Ask: 'Am I reporting from the same time/place?' If yes, keep the word. If no, shift it.

Common mistake: 'He said he was coming tomorrow' (reported next day) × → 'He said he was coming today' ✓

Fun fact: In formal writing, consistent shifting is often preferred even when context allows flexibility! 📚

Pro tip: When in doubt, shift—it's usually safer. Keep original words only when clarity demands it.
examples: Same-day reporting: 'I'll call today' → He said he would call today (if still today).
Same-location: 'This is my office' → She said this was her office (if still in office).
Wrong vs Right: 'She said she is leaving tomorrow' (reported next day) × → 'She said she was leaving today' ✓
functions: Choosing correctly when expressions change vs. stay
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: When in doubt, shift—it's usually safer. Keep original words only when clarity demands it.

lessonActivities.title: Advanced: Complex Time References 🗓️
lessonActivities.content:
Ready for the next level? 🗓️ Reporting speech with complex time references requires careful adjustment of multi-word expressions.

Formation: [Subject] + said + (that) + [complex time-shifted clause]. Example: 'I saw her the day before yesterday' → He said he had seen her two days before.

Use this when:

Direct ExpressionReported ExpressionPattern
the day after tomorrowin two days' time / two days laterSpecific future reference
the day before yesterdaytwo days before / two days earlierSpecific past reference
next week/month/yearthe following week/month/yearRelative future period
last night/week/monththe previous night/week/month / the night/week/month beforeRelative past period
this morning/afternoonthat morning/afternoonSame-day reference shift

Fun fact: 'The day after tomorrow' becomes 'in two days' time'—not 'the day after the day after'! Keep it simple! 🎯

When to use: For multi-word time expressions, shift the entire phrase, not just individual words.
examples: Complex past: 'I saw her the day before yesterday.' → He said he had seen her two days before.
Complex future: 'We'll finish the day after tomorrow.' → She said they would finish in two days' time.
Period reference: 'I traveled last month.' → He said he had traveled the month before.
lessonActivities.tips: When to use: For multi-word time expressions, shift the entire phrase, not just individual words.

lessonActivities.title: Negative Time/Place Shifts ❌
lessonActivities.content:
Let's master the full picture! ❌ Knowing how to report negative statements with time/place expressions completes your control of contextual shifts.

Negative Formation: [Subject] + said/told + (that) + [subject] + didn't/wasn't + [time/place-shifted rest]. Example: 'I'm not here today' → He said he wasn't there that day.

Direct NegativeStructure PatternReported FormShift Applied
Present Simple Neg + Timedon't/doesn't + verb + timedidn't + verb + shifted timetoday→that day, now→then
Present Continuous Neg + Placeam/is/are + not + -ing + placewas/were + not + -ing + shifted placehere→there, this→that
Will Neg + Time/Placewon't + verb + time/placewouldn't + verb + shifted time/placetomorrow→next day, here→there
Can Neg + Contextcan't + verb + contextcouldn't + verb + shifted contextnow→then, here→there

Fun fact: The negation doesn't affect the time/place shift—apply both rules independently! 🔄

Common mistake: 'She said she wasn't here yesterday' × → 'She said she wasn't there the day before' ✓

Remember: In negatives, apply backshift AND time/place shifts: don't→didn't + today→that day, isn't→wasn't + here→there.
examples: Negative + time: 'I don't work here today.' → He said he didn't work there that day.
Negative + place: 'I'm not staying here.' → She said she wasn't staying there.
Negative + future: 'I won't be there tomorrow.' → He said he wouldn't be there the next day.
lessonActivities.tips: Remember: In negatives, apply backshift AND time/place shifts: don't→didn't + today→that day, isn't→wasn't + here→there.

lessonActivities.title: Time/Place Shifts with Time Clauses 🕐⏱️
lessonActivities.content:
Here's a crucial rule! 🕐⏱️ When you use time clauses with time/place expressions in reported speech, both the clause AND the expression may shift!

The Rule: Apply shift rules to time expressions within time clauses just like in main clauses. Example: 'I'll call when I get here tomorrow' → She said she would call when she got there the next day.

Time StarterDirect SpeechReported SpeechShifts Applied
when'I'll call when I arrive tomorrow.'She said she would call when she arrived the next day.tomorrow→the next day
before'Finish before you leave here.'He told me to finish before I left there.here→there
after'I'll call after I get home today.'She said she would call after she got home that day.today→that day
while'Don't talk while I'm speaking here.'He told me not to talk while he was speaking there.here→there

Common mistake: 'She said she would call when she arrives tomorrow' × → 'She said she would call when she arrived the next day' ✓

Fun fact: Time expressions in time clauses follow the same shift rules as in main clauses—just apply them to each part! 🔄

Never forget: After [time words], shift time/place expressions just like in the main clause. Main clause = [shifted], time clause = [shifted].
examples: With 'when': 'I'll call when I arrive here tomorrow.' → She said she would call when she arrived there the next day.
With 'before': 'Finish before you leave today.' → He told me to finish before I left that day.
With 'after': 'I'll call after I get home.' → She said she would call after she got home. (no shift if context unchanged)
functions: Applying shifts to time expressions within time clauses
Managing multiple shifts in complex sentences
lessonActivities.tips: Never forget: After [time words], shift time/place expressions just like in the main clause. Main clause = [shifted], time clause = [shifted].

lessonActivities.title: Mastery: Advanced Contextual Nuances 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
You've come so far! 🎯 Let's tackle the advanced nuances that separate good from great in time/place reporting.

Special Case 1: Mixed Context Reporting

Sometimes one sentence has multiple time/place references from different contexts. Example: 'I was here yesterday, but I'll be there tomorrow' → He said he had been there the day before, but he would be here the next day.

Special Case 2: Formal vs. Informal Register

In formal contexts, use precise shifted expressions. In casual speech, simplify. Formal: 'He stated that he would arrive on the following day.' Casual: 'He said he'd get there tomorrow.'

Context / RegisterPreferred ShiftRhetorical EffectExemplar
Casual SpeechFlexible, clarity-focusedNatural, conversationalHe said he'd call tomorrow.
Formal WritingConsistent shiftingPrecise, professionalHe stated that he would contact me on the following day.
Academic ReportingShifting with hedgingObjective, cautiousThe author reported that the data appeared to support the hypothesis at that time.

Mastery checklist: ✓ Identify all time/place expressions ✓ Apply shifts to each ✓ Check context for exceptions ✓ Adjust for register ✓ Verify clarity

Fun fact: Native speakers often simplify shifts in casual speech—focus on clarity first! 💬

Master level: In formal writing, apply shifts consistently. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!
examples: Mixed contexts: 'I was here yesterday, but I'll be there tomorrow.' → He said he had been there the day before, but he would be here the next day.
Formal shift: 'I'll finish this today.' → He stated that he would complete that task that day.
Casual simplification: 'I saw her here yesterday.' → He said he saw her here yesterday (if context clear).
functions: Using time/place shifts in sophisticated ways
Adapting to different registers and contexts
lessonActivities.tips: Master level: In formal writing, apply shifts consistently. In speech, prioritize clarity: if the meaning is clear, small variations are acceptable!

writingActivities.question: Report what your friend said yesterday about their plans. Include: a time expression change and a place expression change.
writingActivities.hint: Change 'today'→'that day', 'here'→'there'. Example: She said she would meet me there that day.

writingActivities.question: Convert this direct statement to reported speech with time shift: 'I am busy here now.'
writingActivities.hint: Use said/told + backshift 'am' to 'was' and shift 'here' to 'there', 'now' to 'then'. Example: He said he was busy there then.

writingActivities.question: Tell a short story about what your teacher said about an event last week. Use reported speech with time/place shifts at least twice.
writingActivities.hint: Begin with 'The teacher said that last week...'. Add details with the week before and there.
sentenceStarters: First, the teacher said that last week...
Then, she mentioned that the day before...

writingActivities.question: Describe a conversation where someone talked about future plans. Report the plans with correct time expression shifts.
writingActivities.hint: Remember: tomorrow→the next day, next week→the following week. Example: She said she would travel the following week.

writingActivities.question: Compare what two different people said about the same event using reported speech. Show how their time/place references differed.
writingActivities.hint: Use however/although to show contrast between their statements. Add similarly/both if they agreed on something.
sentenceStarters: Both John and Mary said that..., but John added...

writingActivities.question: Write a paragraph reporting a news announcement about an event. Use cause-effect markers and correct time/place shifts.
writingActivities.hint: Start with the cause: because/since/as. Then show the result with shifted time/place: that day/there.

writingActivities.question: Express an opinion about a rule. Report what someone said about it with correct time/place shifts, then give your view.
writingActivities.hint: State your view with I believe/In my opinion. Support it with for example/this is because. Report others with shifted expressions.
sentenceStarters: In my opinion,... because my teacher said that...
I believe that... as my colleague explained...

writingActivities.question: Describe a hypothetical situation using reported conditional speech with correct time/place shifts. Include what someone said would happen if a condition were met.
writingActivities.hint: Use If + past simple, would + base verb in reported form with shifted expressions. Example: She said that if it rained tomorrow, she would stay home.
sentenceStarters: If it rained the next day, I would... he said.
She mentioned that if..., she would...

writingActivities.question: Report a complex conversation involving a statement with past time reference, a future plan, and a place change. Show mastery by using correct shifts for each.
writingActivities.hint: This requires 3 different shifts: past time→earlier reference, future→would + shifted time, here→there. Pay attention to pronoun shifts.
sentenceStarters: Although she said..., he explained that...
When I asked..., she replied that...

writingActivities.question: Write a formal email summarizing a meeting. Use reported speech with correct time/place shifts to convey what colleagues said, with hedging language and polite conclusions.
writingActivities.hint: Maintain formal register: avoid contractions, use passive voice/formal connectors, end with polite closing. Report speech with consistent shifts.
sentenceStarters: One colleague suggested that, given the circumstances...

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct time expression shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw her yesterday.' → Reported: He said he had seen her ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Yesterday' in direct speech usually becomes 'the day before' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct place expression shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Sit here.' → Reported: She told me to sit ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Here' in direct speech usually becomes 'there' in reported speech when location changes.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct 'now' shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm busy now.' → Reported: He said he was busy ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Now' in direct speech usually becomes 'then' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct 'tomorrow' shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'll call tomorrow.' → Reported: She said she would call ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Tomorrow' in direct speech usually becomes 'the next day' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct 'this' shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I like this book.' → Reported: He said he liked ____ book.
gameActivities.hint: 'This' in direct speech usually becomes 'that' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Which expression does NOT change in same-context reporting?
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm busy today.' (reported same day) → Reported: He said he was busy ____.
gameActivities.hint: If reporting on the same day, 'today' can stay 'today'.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct complex time shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw her the day before yesterday.' → Reported: He said he had seen her ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'The day before yesterday' → 'two days before' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the appropriate shift for 'last week':
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I traveled last week.' → Reported: She said she had traveled ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Last week' usually becomes 'the week before' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct combined time/place shift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'll meet you here tomorrow.' → Reported: He said he would meet me ____ ____.
gameActivities.hint: Both place and time shift: here→there, tomorrow→the next day.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct shift for 'next year':
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'We'll finish next year.' → Reported: They said they would finish ____.
gameActivities.hint: 'Next year' usually becomes 'the following year' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct shift for negative time expression:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm not here today.' → Reported: He said he wasn't ____ ____.
gameActivities.hint: Apply both negation and shifts: isn't→wasn't, here→there, today→that day.

gameActivities.question: Advanced: Choose the most precise shift for mixed context:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I was here yesterday, but I'll be there tomorrow.' → Reported: ____
options: He said he had been there the day before, but he would be here the next day.
He said he was here yesterday, but he will be there tomorrow.
He said he had been here the day before, but he would be there tomorrow.
He said he was there yesterday, but he will be here the next day.
correctAnswer: He said he had been there the day before, but he would be here the next day.
gameActivities.hint: Check: past→past perfect, here→there, yesterday→day before, will→would, tomorrow→next day.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct shift for time clause expression:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'll call when I arrive here tomorrow.' → Reported: She said she would call when she arrived ____ ____.
gameActivities.hint: Time expressions in time clauses shift too: here→there, tomorrow→the next day.

gameActivities.question: Select the appropriate form showing no shift for same context:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm here now.' (reported same place/time) → Reported: He says he's ____ ____.
gameActivities.hint: If reporting from same place/time, expressions may not shift.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct complete transformation with multiple shifts:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw this yesterday here, and I'll show that tomorrow there.' → Reported: ____
options: He said he had seen that the day before there, and he would show that the next day there.
He said he saw this yesterday here, and he will show that tomorrow there.
He said he had seen this the day before here, and he would show that tomorrow there.
He said he saw that yesterday there, and he will show this tomorrow here.
correctAnswer: He said he had seen that the day before there, and he would show that the next day there.
gameActivities.hint: Check: this→that, yesterday→day before, here→there, will→would, tomorrow→next day.

quizActivities.question: What happens to 'yesterday' in reported speech?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw her yesterday.' → Reported: He said he had seen her ____.
quizActivities.hint: 'Yesterday' usually becomes 'the day before' in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Time expressions shift in reported speech: 'yesterday' → 'the day before' or 'the previous day'.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses place expression shift?
quizActivities.sentence: Choose the correct option: 'Meet me here.'
options: She told me to meet her there.
She told me to meet her here.
She said me to meet her there.
She told me meet her there.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: She told me to meet her there.
quizActivities.hint: 'Here' usually becomes 'there' in reported speech when location changes.
quizActivities.explanation: Place expressions shift in reported speech: 'here' → 'there' when the reporting location is different.

quizActivities.question: Identify the correct 'now' shift:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm busy now.' → Reported: He said he was busy ____.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Now' shifts to 'then' or 'at that time' in reported speech to reflect the temporal distance.

quizActivities.question: What is the correct reported form for 'tomorrow'?
options: He said he would call the next day.
He said he would call tomorrow.
He said he will call tomorrow.
He said he called the next day.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: He said he would call the next day.
quizActivities.hint: 'Tomorrow' usually becomes 'the next day' in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' or 'the following day' in reported speech. Also, 'will' backshifts to 'would'.

quizActivities.question: Which expression does NOT change in same-context reporting?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm busy today.' (reported same day) → Reported: He said he was busy ____.
quizActivities.hint: If reporting on the same day, 'today' can stay 'today'.
quizActivities.explanation: When the reporting context is the same (same day), time expressions like 'today' may not shift.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses combined time/place shift?
quizActivities.sentence: Choose the correct option: 'I'll meet you here tomorrow.'
options: He said he would meet me there the next day.
He said he would meet me here tomorrow.
He said he will meet me there tomorrow.
He said he would meet me there tomorrow.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: He said he would meet me there the next day.
quizActivities.hint: Both place and time shift: here→there, tomorrow→the next day.
quizActivities.explanation: Combined shifts apply: 'here' → 'there', 'tomorrow' → 'the next day', and 'will' → 'would'.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct shift for 'the day before yesterday':
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I saw her the day before yesterday.' → Reported: He said he had seen her ____.
quizActivities.hint: 'The day before yesterday' becomes 'two days before' in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Complex time expressions shift as a unit: 'the day before yesterday' → 'two days before' or 'two days earlier'.

quizActivities.question: Select the appropriate shift for 'last week':
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I traveled last week.' → Reported: She said she had traveled ____.
quizActivities.hint: 'Last week' usually becomes 'the week before' in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Last week' shifts to 'the week before' or 'the previous week' in reported speech.

quizActivities.question: Which form correctly shows no shift for same context?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm here now.' (reported same place/time) → Reported: He says he's ____ ____.
quizActivities.hint: If reporting from same place/time, expressions may not shift.
quizActivities.explanation: When the reporting context is identical (same place and time), expressions like 'here' and 'now' may not shift.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct shift for negative time expression:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm not here today.' → Reported: He said he wasn't ____ ____.
quizActivities.hint: Apply both negation and shifts: isn't→wasn't, here→there, today→that day.
quizActivities.explanation: Multiple transformations apply: negation (isn't→wasn't), place shift (here→there), and time shift (today→that day).

quizActivities.question: Identify the error in this time/place shift sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: She said that she wasn't here yesterday, but she is there today.
quizActivities.hint: Check both place AND time shifts in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: Two errors: (1) 'here' should shift to 'there' in reported speech. (2) 'yesterday' should shift to 'the day before' or 'the previous day'.

quizActivities.question: Choose the best form to complete the sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: He said that if he ____ enough time, he would travel ____.
quizActivities.hint: This tests reported conditional with time shift.
quizActivities.explanation: Reported conditionals: if + past simple ('had'), would + base verb. Time expressions also shift: 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct advanced time/place shift usage?
options: The researcher stated that the data appeared to support the hypothesis at that time, though further analysis was warranted.
The researcher said the data supports the hypothesis now.
The researcher stated that the data supported the hypothesis then.
The researcher says that the data supports the hypothesis now.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: The researcher stated that the data appeared to support the hypothesis at that time, though further analysis was warranted.
quizActivities.hint: Look for appropriate register, precise vocabulary, and structural complexity.
quizActivities.explanation: Advanced usage requires appropriate register and contextual fit. Option A demonstrates hedging ('appeared to'), formal vocabulary ('warranted'), and precise time reference ('at that time').

quizActivities.question: Identify the stylistic issue in this formal time/place report:
quizActivities.sentence: The committee said they can't approve the proposal here 'cause it's too expensive today.
quizActivities.hint: Formal writing avoids contractions and colloquialisms.
quizActivities.explanation: In formal/academic writing, contractions (can't, 'cause, it's) should be expanded (cannot, because, it is). This maintains professional register and clarity.

quizActivities.question: Choose the most precise hedging expression for academic time/place reporting:
quizActivities.sentence: The study ____ suggest a correlation at that time, though further research is needed.
quizActivities.hint: Academic writing uses hedging to show caution with claims.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Appeared to' provides appropriate hedging for academic claims—confident but not absolute. 'Definitely' and 'is proven to' are too strong without conclusive evidence.

spellingActivities.hint: Subordinating conjunction - shows contrast in reported clauses
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ it was raining, she said she would go out.

spellingActivities.hint: Subordinating conjunction - shows reason in reported explanations
spellingActivities.sentence: He explained that he was late ____ the traffic.

spellingActivities.hint: Transition word - shows contrast between reported statements
spellingActivities.sentence: She said she was tired. ____, she finished her work.

spellingActivities.hint: Transition word - shows result in reported conclusions
spellingActivities.sentence: She studied hard; ____, she passed the exam, he reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Preposition - shows contrast with noun/gerund in reported clauses
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the rain, she said she would go hiking.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal transition - adds supporting information in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: The report stated the plan was efficient. ____, it was cost-effective.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal contrast marker - acknowledges but persists in reported context
spellingActivities.sentence: The odds were against us. ____, we succeeded, she said.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal result marker - shows logical outcome in reported explanations
spellingActivities.sentence: Funding was cut. ____, the project halted, they reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced preposition - formal contrast with noun phrase in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the challenges, the team delivered excellent results, he stated.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced adverb - formal time reference meaning 'until now' in reported context
spellingActivities.sentence: The data, ____ unavailable, now supports the hypothesis, the researcher reported.
